reviews.review: While this may not be one of the best games, it's certainly one of my favorites, it has responsive controls, tons of replay value due to having so many characters and items to unlock and try, and has artifacts that can keep things fresh if you want to spice up the gameplay with things like locking off abilities every minute or having enemies drop bombs on death. the main problems with it are the bugs that can do a lot of things including causing you to spawn inside things when you drop off the map or cause you to just fall through certain parts of the floor and some enemies being FAR more annoying than they should be, like the bugs on the second to last level that just fly around spitting acid at you, though thankfully the acid spitting bugs are only on one level and you don't find glitches that often, i've only found them around 5 times, and i've had hundreds of playthroughs. (most of which were unsuccesful because i'm bad at video games.)
ULTRA MEGA Twisted Mcnasty Nostalgic Joystick Adventure with Friends (or alone!)

This is like Dark Souls. If Dark Souls was still fun. And 2-D. And was a roguelike. And difficult as ♥♥♥♥. You know, maybe it's not actually like Dark Souls and people should stop comparing every game to Dark Souls.

Amazing and witty descriptions are behind every item and monster in this game (You certainly can pierce the heavens).
Epic music orchestrates behind you all through the game (Except when you freeze time).

Monsters on this planet hate you, a lot. And you just might be the bad guy...

But it's fun.

In Risk of Rain, I wasted over 200 hours screaming into the unknown that is this superbely atmospheric pixellated world.

The updates are done, the community is all but dead, and I've long since uninstalled. But that doesn't stop me from rating this 9999/9999. Just don't use Glass and Command more than once, it's like console commands in a Bethesda game.
